profile_text.body:
The Algorithmic Justice League is a nonprofit founded in 2016 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It describes its mission as raising awareness about the impacts of AI, equipping advocates with empirical research, building the voice and choice of the most impacted communities, and galvanizing researchers, policy makers, and industry practitioners to mitigate AI harms and biases. The organization says AI systems are used to decide who gets hired, the quality of medical treatment people receive, and whether someone becomes a suspect in a police investigation, and it argues that unchecked, unregulated, and at times unwanted AI can amplify racism, sexism, ableism, and other forms of discrimination.

Its site highlights a campaign on facial recognition in airports, noting that the TSA is expanding its use of the technology and that travelers can opt out, and it asks people to share their experiences with airport face scans. It also points to the Coded Bias film as the account of how the organization began, describing it as a documentary about people affected by harmful technology and about women sounding the alarm on threats AI poses to civil rights. The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2020. The site asks supporters to become monthly sustainers.

The organization is not recorded as holding any lawsuits, and no AI products are tracked for it. Massachusetts is the jurisdiction listed in connection with it, with a count of 143.
